analysis.title: Raymond James Investment Strategy daily note, Monday, November 16, 2026
key_insights: 3Q26 earnings season is in its final busy week. S&P 500 EPS are on pace to rise 31% YoY, the third straight quarter of growth above 25%.
The beat rate was weak. Firms beat estimates by just 3.3%, the smallest margin since 4Q22, and the S&P 500 is down 3% since earnings season began.
Consensus projects 16% S&P 500 EPS growth in 2027, revised up 1.4% since the start of 4Q.
October headline PPI rose 0.3% MoM, slightly cooler than expected. September was revised up to 1.4% from 1.3%. PPI is up 6.5% YoY, the fastest pace since November 2022.
Core PPI rose 4.9% YoY and has stayed in a 4.8% to 5.0% range for six months, its highest levels since 2022. Goods prices rose 0.5% MoM and services 0.2%.
RJ says the CPI and PPI reports reinforce its expectation for a 25 bp Fed rate hike on December 9.
Last week's inflation data and hawkish Fed comments repriced rates sharply, with more than three hikes now expected by June 2027. The 2-year yield rose 34 bps and the 10-year rose 28 bps to 5.14%.
RJ still expects yields to trend lower over the next year, despite the largest weekly 2-year rise since Oct-24 and the 10-year's biggest weekly rise since April 2025.
Eleven Fed members speak this week, starting with Chair Warsh today at the Fed's conference on Productivity and Jobs.
Retail sales are due tomorrow with consensus at +0.2% MoM. Home Depot reports tomorrow, Target and Lowe's Wednesday, Walmart and Ross Stores Thursday.
Real-time indicators (hotel occupancy, restaurant bookings, department store spending) signal resilient consumer demand despite stubborn inflation.

Aterio forecasts behind-the-meter capacity at data centers rising from 4 GW in 2026 to 188 GW by 2031. Stricter state and city data center rules may require on-site generation, which RJ says should lift demand for electrical equipment and supports its constructive Industrials view.

sector_views.rationale: Behind-the-meter data center power requirements should boost demand for a broad range of electrical equipment.

2027 S&P 500 EPS growth consensus is 16%, revised up 1.4% since the start of 4Q (consensus estimate, not reported).
Retailer earnings upcoming and not yet reported: Home Depot (Tuesday), Target and Lowe's (Wednesday), Walmart and Ross Stores (Thursday).

risk_factors: Stubborn inflation with PPI at four-year highs and core PPI near 5%.
Hawkish Fed repricing, with more than three hikes expected by June 2027.
A thin earnings beat margin, the smallest since 4Q22, alongside a 3% index decline since the season began.
Consumer spending may not carry through year-end, to be tested by this week's retail sales and retailer earnings.
